meta.title: The Paths No One Planned | What 5,680 worn trails say to the people who draw the map
meta.family_reason: One research finding (the first citywide count of desire lines, Foster & Newell 2019) delivered in 90 seconds with the result stated first. D2 was the other candidate, but the film reports who found what and what it changes, not how to recognize a concept. A1/A3 fit a belief-reversal better but are 4 to 6 minute forms.
meta.lead: In Detroit, two researchers mapped the footpaths that no one planned.
meta.logline: Trails worn by walking are not damage to a plan: counted from the air, they are a record of where people need to go, and some planners pave them.
meta.audience_belief: People who cut across the grass are breaking the design.
meta.axis_fact: Virginia Tech said the dirt paths on its Drillfield 'were never a planned feature', and in the summer of 2014 it paved three of them.
meta.materials: (1) Open-license live-action stock footage (Pexels, Pixabay, Mixkit, Coverr): lawns, footpaths, people walking, snow on a square, aerial views. (2) Vector graphics drawn over or beside the footage: paved line vs walked line, schematic maps, typography. No commissioned shooting, no generated images.

sources.label: Foster, A. & Newell, J. P., Detroit's lines of desire: Footpaths and vacant land in the Motor City, Landscape and Urban Planning 189, 260-273, 2019
sources.checked: Abstract (on the authors' institute page, DOI 10.1016/j.landurbplan.2019.04.009): 'more than 5680 of these footpaths, totaling more than 150 miles (>240 km)'; method 'remote sensing and spatial analysis with physical audits and interviews'; desire lines 'visible from space'. Journal highlights (ScienceDirect, seen as a search excerpt) say 'citywide census found 5680 desire lines ... over 150 linear miles'. Discrepancy: 'more than 5680' (abstract) vs '5680' (highlights, press release). The script says 'at least 5,680' and 'more than 150 miles', true under both readings.
sources.status: 직접 확인 (초록과 서지. 논문 본문은 유료라 읽지 못함)

sources.label: University of Michigan News (Michigan News), Visible from outer space, Detroit's unofficial pathways could play important role in land redevelopment, 24 Sep 2019
sources.checked: 'mapped 5,680 unofficial footpaths in the city of Detroit, that's 157 linear miles of trails'; authors Joshua Newell (U-M) and Alec Foster (Illinois State); a marked-up aerial image was used as a guide and students documented sites on the ground in 2013; footpaths are 'residents' way of dealing with this reality, creating shortcuts to school, bus lines and other places they need to go'; the Newell quote on cards c10-c11, word for word.

sources.label: Joel Kurth, In a changing Detroit, footpaths are vanishing across vast, empty lands, Bridge Michigan, 4 Oct 2019
sources.checked: The count is for 2010 ('5,680 footpaths ... totaling 157 miles in 2010'; satellite images of 2010 compared with 2016; footpaths declined 13 percent overall by 2016). 'The informal trails are known by urban planners as desire paths'. Paths run 'across vacant land'. Dissent recorded here: Donna Givens (Eastside Community Network) called the study 'patronizing' and 'a nostalgic, poverty porn exercise'.

sources.label: Virginia Tech News, Dirt paths on Drillfield to be paved, 5 Aug 2014
sources.checked: 'three of the dirt pathways crossing the grass area are paved with asphalt' (announced, work to finish before the fall semester); 'The dirt paths were never a planned feature of the Drillfield. They evolved organically as students crossed the area over time'; the new paths 'will join five existing paved paths', five feet wide against twelve; 'a temporary fix'; reason given: mud tracked into buildings.

sources.label: Virginia Tech News, Students join the team seeking to find a better path across the Drillfield, 8 Dec 2014
sources.checked: Confirms the paving happened: 'Several smaller paths were paved this past summer as a temporary remedy until a more permanent solution could be identified.' Gives 'several', not 'three'. Also 'The larger paths were first paved in the late 1970s' (Virginia Tech Magazine says the first two asphalt walks were poured in 1971; that date is not used).

sources.label: University of Wisconsin-Madison News, Desire paths: the unofficial footpaths that frustrate, captivate campus planners, 24 Apr 2019
sources.checked: Planners 'can either create an official path along it ..., insert an impediment to the alignment, or modify the topography'. Desire paths 'in the winter, are footsteps pressed into snow' (basis for the snow scene on c10-c11; no claim about planners reading snow is made).

sources.label: The State News (Michigan State University student newspaper), Desire paths: how the art of deviant pedestrianism shapes MSU campus, Oct 2023
sources.checked: Campus planner Steve Troost's team has 'two choices when they see a desire path forming: fight or submit': flower beds or post and chain to deter, or a sidewalk laid in its place (Adams Field; Berkey Hall, where the chain came out and a walkway went in).

sources.label: Ohio State University Libraries, University Archives blog, The Oval's Long Walk has paved the way for students for a century, 25 Nov 2014
sources.checked: Not used on screen. Says only that students' walking paths 'partly led to the current design of sidewalks'; the popular version (Ohio State waited and paved whatever students wore) is stronger than this source, so it was left out.

cast.look: One stock clip or still: a small KEEP OFF THE GRASS sign staked in a mown lawn, daylight, sign in the left third of the frame, grass filling the rest.
cast.fixed: The same clip, same framing, is used on c01 and again on c16-c17. The center of the frame stays empty grass so the type has a clear, darkened place.

cast.look: A thin amber vector line, hand-steady, slightly irregular.
cast.fixed: Always and only a path worn by walking. It is drawn progressively, never appears all at once, and it is the only warm color on screen.

cast.look: A clean white vector line, straight or evenly curved, heavier than the amber line.
cast.fixed: Always a paved path. It never means 'planned': the source does not say the older paved paths were planned.

type_style.face: thin white sans-serif for editorial cards; a serif for the quote cards c10-c11
type_style.size: about 5% of frame height (52-56 px at 1080p); two lines, three at most
type_style.em: one weight step heavier, no color change (color is reserved for the amber and white lines)
type_style.ground: stock footage graded down and the center of the frame darkened, so the white type is the brightest thing on screen; diagrams on a dark ground

music_brief.mood: hopeful, gently sentimental, steady and flowing
music_brief.tempo: moderate and even (about 70-90 bpm), a continuous flowing pattern rather than isolated chords
music_brief.avoid: drums and any percussion, vocals, big swells, synthesized stand-ins for a piano
music_brief.pause: none required; if the chosen track has a natural breath, set it under c16

review_notes: stock-heavy (스톡 56%): the brief makes open-license stock footage the main material and allows no shooting. Each stock scene is given a specific job in carries, and the Detroit count, the method, the two choices and the Virginia Tech case are carried by diagrams (7 cards) instead of footage.

Numbers (manual): D1 asks for one or two numbers per film. The script has two figures (5,680 and 150 miles) and one spelled-out count ('three'), kept because 'three' is the axis fact and is what the diagram on c14-c15 shows.

c14 'paved three': three is the number announced by the university on 5 Aug 2014 (S4); its 8 Dec 2014 release (S5) confirms that 'several smaller paths were paved this past summer' without repeating the number. No motive is claimed on screen: the stated reason was mud, and the paving was called temporary.

c10-c11: the quote is the researcher's interpretation, not a measured result, and is shown as a quote for that reason. Bridge Michigan (S3) records a local critic who called the study patronizing; the script therefore says 'across vacant lots' on c08 and does not present the trails as a good in themselves.

Finland snowfall claim (planners visit parks after the first snow): every instance found traces back to a 2011 Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea document quoted second-hand; no Finnish source was found, so it is not used. The snow scene on c10-c11 shows footprints only.
English periods: sentence-final cards carry a period so that the linter can tell closed cards from hand-off cards (see test-log).

Manual check, overlap kept on c13: the diagram shows the same two choices the sentence names. It is kept because it teaches the sign (amber turning white) that c15 relies on; no unsourced extra claim was added to make the picture say more.

Manual check, overlap kept on c07: the picture is a view from above and the sentence says 'overhead images'. The sentence is kept because the picture alone does not say that this was the method, and it carries the two methods that cannot be filmed.
Manual check, axis fact: it sits at 66-76 s (the D1 'meaning' row), not in the middle of the film; the first 57 s belong to the finding. The D1 beat sheet has no earlier slot for it.

Manual check, wording changed after the first lint run: sources call the imagery 'aerial' (press release), 'satellite' (Bridge) and 'remote sensing' (abstract), so the screen says 'overhead images' and the label says '2010 imagery'; 'vacant lots' became 'vacant land' to match the sources.
Manual check, c10-c11: snow is brighter than white type. The clip must be overcast or dusk and graded down, or the quote will not read.

Editor pass after skill 0.6.0: every live-action card here is a stand-in (스톡): the study's own imagery and the Drillfield are not available as open footage. The stock-heavy warning (56%) is therefore accurate and is kept. If this script goes to production, the first fix is to license or redraw the study's map so that the finding is shown, not suggested.
Editor pass: the source label was moved from c02 (stand-in footage of walking feet) to c04 (the map diagram), so no stand-in shot carries a year.
assumptions: No title card: family D1 states the result on the first text card.
All non-screen fields (visual.desc, carries, notes) are written in English because the production crew and the stock search work in English; enum values stay in Korean as the data spec requires.
The KEEP OFF THE GRASS sign stands for the audience belief; it is shown, never quoted in a sentence.

beats.name: 발견
beats.job: State the finding first: who mapped what, where, and the one condition that makes it odd (no one planned them).
beats.scene: The rule (a sign on a lawn), then feet crossing grass. The worn trail itself is not shown yet.
beats.text: Who, where, and that the paths were unplanned.

beats.name: 규모
beats.job: Give the size of the finding: how many and how long.
beats.scene: How scattered and how dense: lines filling a schematic city map.
beats.text: The two figures, one per card.

beats.name: 근거
beats.job: Say how the count was made.
beats.scene: What a worn trail looks like from above, next to a paved one. First full view of the object.
beats.text: The three methods; only the aerial one can be shown.

beats.name: 기제
beats.job: Say why the trails exist: who wore them and to get where.
beats.scene: Ordinary people on foot on a bare-earth trail; then the same kind of line written in snow in a day.
beats.text: The cause (shortcuts), the ground (vacant lots), the destinations, and the researcher's reading in his own words.

beats.name: 의미
beats.job: Say what changes: the trails have a name, planners have a choice, and one university paved three.
beats.scene: The choice as two states of one line (blocked, paved); then three walked lines becoming paved lines on one field.
beats.text: The name, the choice, and who paved how many, where and when.

beats.name: 마지막
beats.job: Turn the subject to 'we' and the tense to the future, and take back 'no one planned' from the lead.
beats.scene: The sign from the first shot again, now read with the film behind it.
beats.text: One line with 'we' and 'will'. No new fact.

beats.name: 참고 자료
beats.job: Name the study and the two official releases the film rests on.
beats.text: Authors, journal, year, and the two news offices.

cards.label: Detroit · 2010 imagery · Foster & Newell, 2019

visual.desc: Dark schematic street-grid map of a city, no labels and no counter. Thin amber lines appear one after another in the gaps of the grid.

cards.note: Illustrative only, not data: do not trace a real map of Detroit and do not let the number of amber lines read as a count. Wording: the abstract says 'more than 5680', the highlights and the press release say '5,680'; 'at least' is true under both. The count is for 2010 (S3); the label says 'imagery' because sources differ on aerial vs satellite.

visual.desc: (continues) The amber lines keep accumulating until the grid is laced with them; then the street grid dims and only the amber lines remain.
visual.carries: The trails as one body of line, which the sentence measures.

cards.note: Abstract: 'more than 150 miles (>240 km)'; press release: '157 linear miles'. 'More than 150 miles' is true under both. Illustrative diagram, not data.
